name: card
purpose: Surface: a bordered, token-colored panel (flat, raised, sunken, optionally padded). Card: a surface with header (title, subtitle), media, body, and footer sections; an <article> named by its title when titled, and an optional block-link mode where the whole card is clickable with a single tab stop.
whenToUse: Grouping a self-contained piece of content: a product, project, article teaser, or summary tile.
Collections of similar items in a grid, each linking to a detail page (interactive cards).
Panels that visually separate a region of a page (Surface).
whenNotToUse: A single clickable action without content: use a Button or Link.
Cards with several equally important actions: do not use interactive mode; put actions in the footer instead.
Tabular or comparable data across items: use a table.
responsive: Cards fill their container inline size; put them in an aui-grid--auto grid for responsive collections. Footer content wraps. Media images are fluid (inline-size 100%).
rtl: Logical properties throughout; header, body, and footer content follow the writing direction.
theme: color-surface, color-surface-sunken, color-border, radius-md, shadow-sm (raised), shadow-md (interactive hover), space-inset (density-aware). Interactive titles use color-link. Forced-colors mode keeps the border, uses LinkText for the title link, and a Highlight focus outline.
security: Title, subtitle, and string content use textContent; Node content is appended as-is (the consumer owns it). interactive.href is validated with the WHATWG URL parser and must be http(s) or relative; javascript:, data:, and other schemes are rejected, including obfuscated forms. No inline styles. CSP-safe.
dataHandling: No persistence, network access, or telemetry.

performance.testedScale: Constant DOM per card (root plus five section elements) and one configuration subscription; no event listeners. Not yet part of the e2e performance suite.

limitations: In interactive cards, the link overlay makes body text hard to select with the mouse (a known trade-off of the block-link pattern).
Other controls inside an interactive card are lifted above the overlay and remain separate tab stops.
The card root element is replaced when a title is added or removed, because the tag changes between <article> and <div>.
Surface and Card do not manage elevation stacking contexts.
unsupported: HTML strings as title, subtitle, or content (pass a Node instead).
Buttons (non-link actions) as the whole-card target.
antiPatterns: Wrapping a whole card in an <a>: screen readers announce all of its content as the link name.
Interactive cards without a descriptive title.
Heading levels that skip the surrounding outline; set headingLevel to match the page.

adapters.angular: @absoluteui/angular/card: AuiCard directive ([auiCard]); no directive for Surface.apply (use the aui-surface classes).
